expected_execution_change: Direction: the type term (weight 0.3) supplies the categorical element signal at the two typed slots, steering slot 12 toward N and slot 22 toward C, while the half term (weight 0.7) supplies the geometric/context signal on the fixed support. Endpoint, orientation, pair and role weights are zero and therefore inactive; no anchor is present, so no anchor term contributes. Dose is the frozen calibration dose (max_atom_step_A 0.15, max_cumulative_rms_A 6.0, native_rms_ratio 0.66, pointcloud_delta_A 1.0) with native options cat_noise_euler_guard false, cat_noise_level 1.0, coord_noise_level 0.2, final_corr_pred true, use_sde_simulation true. The expected measurable response is a change in the realized typed-slot element probabilities and in the final generated-parent affinity relative to the L109 parent baseline (mean 7.7985, best_qualified 8.1324), with quality side effects (assignment switching, joint formation, retention) reported. Because the type term is a relative mixture weight, the direction is steered by the 0.7/0.3 split while the actual dose is set separately by the frozen calibration parameters; scaling all weights would cancel under normalization and is not the intervention.
falsifier: The relocation hypothesis is rejected if, at the frozen calibration dose, the measured generated-parent affinity for the L110 layout does not exceed the L109 parent's measured mean 7.7985 / best_qualified 8.1324, or if the realized typed-slot element probabilities at slots 12 and 22 do not shift toward N and C respectively (i.e., the type term produces no measurable injection/formation change at those slots). A further falsifier is that the joint layout contrast fails to favor L110 over L109 at this fixed support, or that the swap is shown not to be locally compatible. If the falsifier fires, the native L109 layout should be retained. This falsifier concerns measured execution and terminal outputs, not whether a static input file changes its original labels or source score.
scientific_rationale: L110 is a legal fixed-support relabel of the native L109 layout: the same 20-point support and the same two typed slots (12, 22), with the neutral degree-two pyridine-type aromatic N / aromatic CH exchange class preserved at both sites. The only free quantity is the label layout at those two slots; region discovery is frozen and the extra context points receive direct geometry loss. Site evidence supports local compatibility of the swap: slot 12 (C->N) has N_minus_C 0.3068 with a negligible best-donor strength (1.55e-06 at A:ASP:175:N), so the added N is not penalized by donor proximity; slot 22 (N->C) has N_minus_C 0.0763 with a strong donor (A:VAL:116:N, strength 0.951), and removing the acceptor at a site whose native element is N is consistent with the donor environment. The joint layout contrast favors L110 (8.912224) over native L109 (8.704859), and L110 is the top-ranked of the 10 measured legal layouts. I explicitly do not treat 8.912224 as a generation forecast: it is a teacher layout score for the source input, and the discriminating outcome is the measured generated-parent affinity. The prior rounds R01-R04 varied native_rms_ratio and weights but never changed the label layout, so they are not a control for this relocation; R04 was rolled back. V00 is the only allowed variant and is untested at this exact label layout, which is the reason to run it prospectively.
